children.value: Contributing to Kirana

Thank you for wanting to help. Kirana is small and independent, so every good
bug report, docs fix and pull request moves it noticeably. This page says what
helps most and how to get a change merged without a round of back-and-forth.
The same guide is

in the repository, and the ways to support
the project with money are on the
sponsors page
Report a bug
The most valuable contribution at this stage. A good report has:
What you ran

: the Kirana version, your framework and bundler, and the
smallest source that shows the problem.
What you expected and what happened

: the computed style you expected,
and the one you got.

prints every
entry for a style and the one that won; paste its output.
The diagnostic
, if there was one, with its code (

A style that compiles and renders wrong is a bug even when no diagnostic fired;
report it. So is a diagnostic whose help text did not tell you what to do.
Improve the docs

If a page made you guess, it is wrong. Open an issue naming the page and the
sentence, or send the fix. Docs live in
; run
in

after editing, so the generated pages and the
search index follow.

Every statement in the docs should be true of the code today. A claim about
performance, size or another project needs a source or a measurement beside it.
Change the code
Before you start
Open an issue first

for anything beyond a small, obvious fix, and wait for a
maintainer to agree on the approach. It saves you writing a pull request that
cannot be merged. Pull requests that only reformat, rename or reorder code are
not accepted: the formatters and linters own that.
Set up

properties.source:
vp install             # dependencies, and the git hooks
vp run check           # format, lint, types, docs consistency
vp run rust            # cargo fmt, Clippy, cargo-deny, Rust tests
vp run test            # Vitest
vp run build           # native engine, then the docs site

What a pull request needs
Tests, and 100 % coverage.

Kirana's packages keep 100 % coverage of Rust
lines, functions and regions, and of TypeScript statements, branches, functions
and lines.
checks it. A change that lowers it fails CI.
The specification, in the same change.

A change to the compiler's
behaviour updates the matching document in

, and a design choice gets
a decision in
The docs, in the same change.

A new token, diagnostic, option or
behaviour is not finished until
says so.
Evidence for a trade-off.

If your change makes something worse to make
something else better, show the failing case, the numbers and a test.
A sign-off on every commit.

Security
Do not change files under

in the same pull request as
other work; a workflow change is reviewed on its own.
Report a vulnerability privately, never in a public issue: see

CI actions and runner images are pinned to an exact version, never written
from memory: check the action's latest release and that it runs on a
supported runtime.
Support the project
Kirana is MIT licensed and free to use. If it saves you time,
the sponsors page

lists every way to support it (GitHub Sponsors,
Open Collective, Polar, and invoices for companies) once each channel opens.
Conduct

Be kind, be specific, and assume good intent. Critique code and ideas, never
